Subject: Outstanding invoice + remit clarification / escalation

Hi Oliver / Graybridge billing team,

Hope you’re well. I wanted to follow up on Invoice 4498 (attached) — it’s now 34 days past due. Per our records the invoice was issued 2026-12-14 for $148,500 USD. We’ve had earlier email threads but haven’t received confirmation of payment or a PO match.

Two items blocking payment clearance on our side:
- Your AP referenced PO 7782 in a note, but the PO on file (attached) is for a different entity name and has a different billing reference. Can you confirm which entity will remit?
- We have not received VAT/withholding evidence your treasury mentioned in the procurement call. For EU VAT reverse-charge or any cross-border tax paperwork we need the supporting docs to clear tax hold.

We’re keen to avoid taking any action that interrupts service. That said, if we don’t receive a cleared payment instruction or a confirmed staged remit plan by end-of-day 2027-01-22 (PST), we’ll need to escalate to a temporary remit block per collections policy and loop in leadership for a credit hold decision.

Next steps requested: please confirm (1) paying entity and remittance bank/ACH details, (2) if you’ll provide the VAT/withholding evidence and expected delivery date, and (3) whether Graybridge can commit to a staged payment (50% now, balance within 30 days) if the full payment cannot be made immediately.

Attachments: Invoice_4498.pdf, Graybridge_PO_7782.pdf

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Receivable Manager
Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com | M: +1 415-555-0199
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@graybridge.com>

Evelyn — thanks for the flag and apologies for the delay.

Short answers:
1) Paying entity: Graybridge Global Services Ltd — we will remit from the UK treasury, but the PO was issued by Graybridge Inc. (US). Treasury is coordinating an inter-entity transfer and we expect funds to be available, but they need VAT reverse-charge confirmation to process without additional tax withholdings.
2) VAT evidence: attaching a preliminary VAT letter; full documentation takes a few business days from our tax team.
3) Staged payment: we can do 40% by 01/25 and the remainder by 02/24 if that works for Redwood.

We’d like to avoid service interruption — can you confirm you’ll accept the 40/60 staged plan while we finish the VAT paperwork? If Redwood needs exec sign-off, let me know and I’ll escalate internally to our CFO.

Attachments: VAT_prelim_letter.pdf

—Oliver
Oliver Park

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding Graybridge response. They propose 40% on 01/25 and remainder by 02/24, and say VAT docs are in progress. They’re asking whether we’ll accept staged remit while their tax team completes paperwork.

My read: low immediate risk of non-payment, but inter-entity complexity means collection could be slow; they explicitly said they will escalate to CFO if we require exec commitment. Two questions for collection stance:
1) Approve staged remit (40/60) and hold off on remit-block/action pending proof of first payment on 01/25?
2) If we accept staged remit, do we require a signed mutual action plan and a DocuSign commitment (we can attach a 2-line payment commitment to the invoice) to mitigate risk?

If leadership wants to pressure for earlier payment, I can request a CFO call and offer to withhold service warnings only on missed 01/25 milestone (i.e., escalate on first miss).

—Eve

Eve — thanks for the summary. Approve staged remit acceptance with conditions:
- Require a signed payment commitment (DocuSign) for the 40% due 2027-01-25 and the remaining 60% due 2027-02-24. I want payment triggers and a late fee clause (standard).
- Require a VAT evidence ETA (they said few business days) — set a firm follow-up date 2027-01-29. If no VAT evidence by that date, escalate to me; we will then consider a temporary remit block.
- If the 01/25 payment does not land, authorize immediate service warning and schedule an exec touchpoint w/ me and their CFO for next business day.

Karthik — please prep a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) with the two payment dates + DocuSign wrapper. Put it in Sales>Deals>GB-49 and share the Drive link with Eve by EOD.

Kimberly Park
VP, Credit & Collections
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Outstanding invoice + remit clarification / escalation — MAP and next steps

Oliver — thanks for the prompt turnaround and for the VAT prelim. Per Kimberly’s guidance we’ll accept the staged remit with the following conditions:
1) We need a signed mutual action plan (attached brief MAP) via DocuSign that commits Graybridge to: 40% payment ($59,400 USD) by 2027-01-25 and remaining 60% ($89,100 USD) by 2027-02-24. The MAP includes a standard 1.5% monthly late fee and an acknowledgement that failure to pay the first tranche triggers an immediate service-warning and exec call.
2) Please upload the VAT supporting documentation to the linked shared drive by 2027-01-29: https://drive.redwood/GB-49/VAT-evidence (I’ve added your billing contact).
3) Payment instructions: we will accept wire or ACH to the account listed on the invoice; please confirm payer entity on the signed MAP so accounting can reconcile.

If you can sign the DocuSign by EOD today we will mark the invoice as "staged remit — protected" and pause any remit block actions. If we do not receive the signed MAP or the first payment by 2027-01-25 17:00 PST, we will put an immediate remit block and schedule an exec call between Kimberly, our legal, and Graybridge CFO.

Attachments: MAP_4498_StagedRemit.docx, Invoice_4498.pdf

Appreciate your cooperation — looking forward to the signature.

Best,
